question_type: 5-value time series from a pinned issue (OFS-2 mutual funds, end-March 2000-2004) -> one-year 99% VaR-style tail loss, converted to JPY with an FX rate that is not in the corpus (FRED-style monthly average)
decisive_step: Two decisions stack. (1) CELL_SELECTION: in treasury_bulletin_2010_03.txt:1869 the OFS-2 header carries 13 labels for 12 numeric columns (a parent-only 'Pension funds 3 > Unnamed: 8_level_1' label with no ordinal), so every label right of it sits one column too far right; the mutual-funds series is the 9th numeric column, i.e. the column show_table labels 'Insurance companies 3 (8)', not the one it labels 'Mutual funds 3,7 (9)'. The reference pinned this with the identity 'columns (4)..(12) sum to column (3)' (worklog Step 3, treasury_bulletin_2010_03.txt:1871; review.md check 2). (2) The metric convention and the FX source: the reference chose parametric-normal VaR with mean, sample sd, simple returns, scaled by the latest holdings, and an EXTERNAL (recalled FRED EXJPUS monthly-average) rate because the corpus only has point-in-time FCP-II rates (worklog Steps 4 and 6) -- and was still graded wrong (correct.opus = 0), so the convention the key uses is unknown. Every GLM cell used the corpus month-end FCP-II-2 rate instead, which the reference's own sensitivity table shows moves the result by ~4%.

It then fell into a 13-step loop (find_tables x3, show_table x2 on FCP-II-2, rg) repeated ~41 times from a[14] to a[545] (301 requests, 36M input tokens, 46 min) until a Codex compaction; after the compaction it re-derived the same series (a[551]-a[553]), used the corpus month-end FCP-II-2 rate, and at a[571] computed an ad-hoc 'latest level minus lowest level' loss.

smallest_change.change: show_table (otables.py ~line 1150, the branch that emits 'the LAST labelled column(s) ... never hold data: the header probably has a spurious extra label'): instead of only warning, realign the labels when the header can be pinned. Rule: if the header has k+1 labels for k data-bearing columns, and the labels carry ordinals '(1)'..'(k)' with exactly one unnumbered (parent-only) label, drop the unnumbered label and shift the labels right of it one column left; confirm with the identity (c3 = sum c4..c12) and, when available, a sibling printing whose header is not shifted. Print in COLUMNS the realigned mapping and a flag, e.g.: `v8 = c8 Insurance companies 3 (8) [num] [LABELSHIFT-1]`, `v9 = c9 Mutual funds 3,7 (9) [num] [LABELSHIFT-1]`, ..., and in NOTES: `- header had 13 labels for 12 numeric columns: the unnumbered label 'Pension funds 3' (a parent header with no child) was dropped and labels (8)-(12) moved one column left; identity c3 = sum c4..c12 holds on 39/39 rows with this mapping; 2010_06:1794 prints the same numbers under 'Mutual funds' at c9`. Apply the same realignment inside printings so that, for a row/column, the per-issue values form one run instead of two conflicting runs with ISOLATED warnings (b2[43], c[99]); when the two runs cannot be reconciled, printings should say which issues have a shifted header rather than 'likely OCR/row shift'.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: the realignment only triggers when a trailing labelled column is empty in every row, the ordinal count equals the data-column count and the identity holds after the shift; the old note stays when any of these fails

In b[49] the answer was the rounded loss printed on the same line as the -0.05 quantile it was 'x100' of; the offer was accepted and replaced one wrong value with another.

Only c, which read the raw header and summed the row (c[93]-c[97]), found the column, and it took ~10 steps. A tool that prints the corrected label removes the need for that reasoning.
fix.irreducible: Largely yes for the final answer: (1) the question's FX rate ('monthly, not seasonally adjusted, reported on the first day of the month') is the FRED EXJPUS monthly average, which is not in the corpus (the corpus has only FCP-II point-in-time rates); without web access GLM can only use the corpus month-end rate, which the reference's sensitivity check shows is ~4% off; (2) the metric convention (mean vs zero-mean, sample vs population sd, simple vs log returns, historical vs parametric) is not pinned by the wording, and the reference's best-guess convention with the external rate was still graded wrong, so no arm has ever been right on this question (v8 none/prompt/cards, opus, a, b, b2, c all 0). The column-shift fix is worth making for the many OFS-2 questions, not for this one.

notes: (1) The OFS-2 header in the 2007_03..2010_03 issues has a parent-only 'Pension funds 3 > Unnamed' label with no ordinal; show_table detects the trailing empty column and prints a warning plus the identity, but keeps the wrong labels, and printings then matches by label text, so for one row it reports two value runs (label-column run in 2007_03..2010_03 vs the true series in 2006_09 and 2010_06..2010_12) with ~8 ISOLATED 'likely OCR/row shift' warnings -- the disagreement is real but attributed to the wrong cause (b2[43], c[29], c[99]). The ordinals '(1)'..'(12)' in the labels are the cheapest pin: 12 numbered labels for 12 numeric columns. (2) Cell a shows the text arm has no loop protection: the same 13 commands with identical outputs ran ~41 times (2790 s, 36M input tokens) until Codex compacted; the mech arms' loop_threshold 3 is worth keeping as a control in v10. (3) The 'scale' submit rule produced a false positive in b[49]: it matched the answer against a different number printed by the same multi-line calc, and the model accepted the offer without checking; rules that offer a substitute should first check whether the answer already equals a printed/rounded output of that calc. (4) The 'grounded' rule flagged the normal quantile constant 2.3263... as 'a value no tool output showed' (b, checks 001/002): mathematical constants should be whitelisted or a `calc --quantile` helper should print them. (5) scipy is absent in the workspace (a[558], b[43], b2[39], c[55] all exit 1); statistics.NormalDist works -- the README could say so, or calc could provide z-quantiles. (6) show_table --grep with a value containing spaces failed twice in c (c[12], c[33]); the README example should show the quoting. (7) All four cells searched ~15-25 steps for an exchange-rate table that does not exist; a corpus-level note ('the only FX rates in the corpus are the FCP-II report-date rates; there is no monthly-average series') would have saved most of that, but would not have produced the FRED value.
